timeline.event: Release 9.39.8 of the checkout API starts rolling out to production.
Error rates on the checkout API begin to climb.
The CheckoutErrorRateHigh alert fires and pages the on-call engineer.
Ines Varga acknowledges the page and opens an incident channel.
The team decides to roll back release 9.39.8.
The rollback completes and error rates return to baseline.
Kenji Moreau declares the incident resolved after monitoring stays clean.

root_cause: Release 9.39.8 lowered the database connection-pool limit, so checkout requests queued and timed out under normal weekday load.
contributing_factors: The pool limit was changed in a shared config file without a review from the payments team.
The canary stage ran at off-peak traffic, so the queueing never showed before full rollout.
went_well: The rollback runbook worked first time.
The incident channel kept a clear written timeline.
went_badly: Nobody owned the shared config file that changed.
The status page was updated well after customers started reporting errors.

action_items.action: Lower the alert threshold and add a second, symptom-based alert
Add a review rule for changes to the shared config file
Run canary stages at peak traffic, not off-peak
